matches.rationale: No finding mentions the ambiguous LSE expression or the improperly defined vector exponentiation in Theorem 3.2, so the mathematical inconsistency is not captured.

The ground truth error concerns oversimplification and omitted assumptions in the lower bound of Theorem 3.3, while Finding 2 claims the theorem lacks a formal mathematical statement, which is a different issue.
No finding addresses unfair hyperparameter tuning, larger network sizes, or biased checkpointing that favor the proposed method over baselines.
There is no finding about exaggerated claims or omitted caveats in the abstract; none of the predicted findings mention the abstract at all.

The rhetorical bias in the introduction overstating state entropy's benefits is not identified by any finding; the only introduction-related finding concerns a miscitation, not the unbalanced presentation.
No finding points to selective horizon ranges, sub-sampled seeds, sparse error bars, or omission of failure modes in Figures 4 and 5.
The omission of ethical or reproducibility statements in the experiments is not flagged by any finding.
The fabricated or misused references [5,22] in related work are not called out; Finding 5 concerns a different reference [6] and a different context.
No finding discusses the contradiction between Theorem 3.3's claim about policy entropy weakening guarantees and the experimental evidence that combined entropy often helps.

Finding 3 correctly identifies the flawed proof in Theorem 4.1, noting the insufficiency of a constant-reward symmetrization argument to support the strong impossibility claim, which matches the ground truth error about an oversimplified proof that overstates the result.
No finding detects the manipulation of the low-rollout success rate of state entropy relative to policy entropy in the experiments.
The omission of practical limitations and deployment caveats in the conclusion is not addressed by any finding.
